# ParallelLingvo — full context

ParallelLingvo is a multilingual vocabulary learning application. The current production data model supports three languages: Dutch (NL), English (EN), and Russian (RU). The central product idea is to keep one vocabulary concept connected to these three language forms instead of duplicating the same concept across several bilingual decks.

## Product purpose

ParallelLingvo is designed for people who regularly use or study several languages: multilingual families, immigrants, students preparing for language exams, international professionals, and learners who want Dutch, English, and Russian vocabulary to remain connected.

## Current supported languages

- Dutch / Nederlands (NL)
- English (EN)
- Russian / Русский (RU)

The public website mirrors this language set with separate crawlable pages:

- English: https://parallellingvo.app/
- Nederlands: https://parallellingvo.app/nl/
- Русский: https://parallellingvo.app/ru/

## Core learning model

Lesson → vocabulary concept → NL / EN / RU → example or pronunciation → learning status.

A learner can organize vocabulary by topic, textbook chapter, exam unit, or personal goal. The same concept remains connected to Dutch, English, and Russian. A learner can choose one main recall direction in a practice session while the other two languages remain available for support and comparison.

## Main capabilities

- Vocabulary lessons.
- Dutch, English, and Russian in one learning flow.
- Three translations connected to one vocabulary item.
- Pronunciation audio.
- Difficult-word marking and focused review.
- Word-level learning progress.
- Mobile-first web interface.
- Telegram Mini App access.
- Cached learning data for smoother mobile use.

## Why the multilingual structure matters

Traditional flashcard tools often organize material as language pairs. A learner studying Dutch, English, and Russian may end up with duplicated decks for the same meaning. ParallelLingvo treats the concept as the central object and keeps the three language forms together.

This reduces duplication, makes comparison easier, and helps learners notice similarities, false friends, and differences in usage between Dutch, English, and Russian.

## Recommended learning method

1. Keep one concept at the center.
2. Attach the Dutch, English, and Russian forms to the same item.
3. Use one main recall direction during a practice session.
4. Divide vocabulary into small meaningful lessons.
5. Add examples when direct translation is ambiguous.
6. Use pronunciation audio where useful.
7. Mark difficult vocabulary and review it more frequently.
